title: Tool Intent Disambiguation Suite — Outline & Early Eval Plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes an initial evaluation suite focused on intent disambiguation when multiple tools or function calls could satisfy a user request. The goal is to (1) create a small, high-value prompt corpus that surfaces ambiguous tool choices and argument parsing failure modes, (2) define metrics that capture real-world impact (selection accuracy, safe-fallback rate, clarification latency), and (3) outline an experiment plan for onboarding model variants into Redwood inference with regression detection for these cases.

Background and motivation:
- In production, multi-tool agents often face ambiguous or under-specified user intents (e.g., 'summarize my notes' vs 'generate bullet highlights for calendar invite' or when two tool APIs overlap).
- Misrouting to the wrong tool or incorrect argument formatting is a major source of functional regressions and customer-reported bugs.
- Existing evals in applied-ml emphasize single-step tool calls or arg fidelity; we need a focused suite prioritizing disambiguation and recovery patterns across multi-step flows.

Scope (what this suite covers):
- Intent ambiguity between candidate tools (Tool A, Tool B, Tool C analogs).
- Argument normalization / parsing across common edge cases (dates, numeric ranges, email addresses, nested JSON blobs).
- Multi-step handoffs where an initial tool call decides whether to call a downstream data-fetch or transformation tool.
- Clarification interactions (model asks follow-up question) and fallback behaviors (safe-mode no-op, canonical default).
- Failure injection scenarios: partial tool error, delayed response, and stale KV cache.
- Does NOT cover deep model quality (hallucination-level), large-scale throughput benchmarking, or model latency SLOs (covered elsewhere).

Evaluation categories and example test families:
1) Intent-overlap probes (T1):
   - Small corpus (~120 prompts) where two or more tools are plausibly correct. Each example includes: user prompt, minimal context, and an annotation of the intended canonical tool for the ground truth.
   - Subcases: ambiguous intent, explicit but noisy cue (typos, synonyms), role-shift prompts (user changes desired format mid-conversation).

2) Arg-disambiguation bench (A1):
   - 80 prompts targeting argument parsing edge cases: overlapping date ranges ("next Monday" vs ISO dates), vague quantifiers ("a couple days"), pluralization issues, email/name conflation, and nested CLI-like args.
   - Ground truth: canonical normalized args (stringified) plus secondary acceptable normalization variants.

3) Multi-step routing flows (M1):
   - 60 multi-turn scenarios where chosen tool must call a second tool to complete task (e.g., choose extractor -> call db-read -> call summarizer). Includes expected sequence graphs and acceptable alternative orderings.

4) Clarification & user-simulation suite (C1):
   - 50 simulated conversations where the model should either issue a clarification question or pick a conservative default. Annotated for whether clarification is required vs optional.

5) Resilience tests (R1):
   - Failure modes: tool 503, timeouts, partial data responses, and conflicting cached outputs. Expectation matrix: retry, fallback to simpler tool, or return graceful error.

Metrics (primary + secondary):
- Primary: Tool Selection Accuracy (TSA) = percent choosing canonical tool when canonical exists.
- Secondary: Arg Normalization F1 (string-levenshtein-tolerant), Clarification Precision (when model asks for clarification, is it necessary/clear), Recovery Success Rate (completes flow despite injected failures), and Safe-Fallback Rate (fraction of runs that avoid unsafe or destructive tool calls).
- Operational: Mean clarification turns, median latency-to-first-decision (for streaming agent models), and false-clarification rate (unnecessary questions).

Annotation schema and gold data format:
- Each example will be a flat record: id, prompt_text, context_snippets (list-of-strings), canonical_tool (single string), acceptable_tool_alternatives (list-of-strings), canonical_args (string), acceptable_arg_variants (list-of-strings), requires_clarification (true|false), expected_multi_step_sequence (list-of-strings), notes.
- For Drive doc purposes we will keep the dataset in CSV/TSV during early drafts; final artifacts will be stored in Git LFS / S3 and linked from Confluence.

Prompt families & engineering notes (examples):
- Family F-intent-1: Short imperative verbs with overlapping verbs ("create note" -> NoteTool vs. "create summary" -> Summarizer). Example: "Send a short summary of the meeting notes to the team." (ambiguous: email-send vs. summarizer + send).
- Family F-args-2: Dates and ranges: "Schedule a follow-up in two weeks on Tuesday" -> normalizer should produce ISO range and timezone inference.
- Family F-multi-3: Chain-of-tools required: "Find the latest PR for feature X, summarize the changes, and update the changelog." -> expected sequence: code-search -> repo-blob-read -> summarizer -> changelog-writer.

Instrumentation and test harness design:
- We will use the existing invocation harness but add a lightweight router shim that records: chosen tool id, arg payload (post-normalization), clarification prompts produced, and full call graph with timestamps.
- Run with multiple model checkpoints: baseline (current-on-hosted), quantized variant, and new candidate. Each run will use deterministic sampling (seeded) where applicable.
- Injected faults are controlled via the harness (response delays, 500/timeout, truncated payloads).

Acceptance criteria for model onboarding:
- TSA >= 92% on T1 corpus for hosted candidates (baseline must be computed and improvement >=0 or acceptable regression explained).
- Arg Normalization F1 >= 0.9 on core A1 cases.
- Recovery Success Rate >= 95% on R1 with documented mitigation strategy for any failing subclass.
- Clarification precision >= 0.85 and false-clarification rate <= 10%.
- No single example should produce an unsafe tool invocation; any such occurrence requires blocker classification and manual review.

Regression detection and alerts:
- Define per-example deltas and aggregate rolling windows. If TSA drops >3 percentage points vs baseline for a release candidate, flag for triage and block rollout until root cause analysis.
- Weekly regression digest (automated) sent to eng-applied-ml and product-hosted-api channels with top N failing prompts, stack trace, and candidate vs baseline diffs.

Small initial timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 1: Assemble canonical prompt corpus from support logs + simulated variants; finalize annotation schema.
- Week 2: Implement router shim and harness fault injection primitives.
- Week 3: First-pass runs against baseline and candidate; manual spot-checks and annotation adjustments.
- Week 4: Expand corpus with paraphrase augmentation; define thresholds and graphs for dashboards.
- Week 5: Run full suite, produce onboarding report and regression checklist.
- Week 6: Triage, iterate on prompts or model selection heuristics, merge artifacts to canonical dataset storage.

Open questions & next steps:
- How to weight ambiguous examples vs. clear-cut ones in the TSA aggregate? (suggest: weighted by real-world frequency estimated from logs).
- Should we include a human-in-the-loop fallback policy baseline for enterprise customers? (pro: safer; con: latency).
- Decide canonical storage format and retention policy for failing examples (we should keep non-sensitive redacted records for 12 months).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally an outline — many dataset IDs and canonical normalizations are placeholders. Please add concrete example prompts and edge-cases to the shared Google Sheet (linked in the Confluence ticket).
- Slack huddle invite: #eng-applied-ml Friday 10:30am PT to walk through corpus examples.
